descriptionChirho: A divinely sent plague or epidemic, typically as judgment. This is the primary sense of negef, denoting mass affliction or pestilence. Multilingual evidence strongly supports this medical/disaster reading: eng 'plague', spa 'plaga', hin 'विपत्ति', arb 'الْوَبَاءُ/وَبَاءٌ' (epidemic), kor '역병/재앱' (pestilence), swa 'pigo/tauni' (plague/epidemic). Used predominantly in Exodus and Numbers plague narratives.

A stumbling or cause of tripping, used in the sense of a physical blow or obstacle that causes one to fall. This secondary sense of negef refers to stumbling rather than epidemic. Multilingual evidence confirms the distinct meaning: eng 'striking', spa 'tropiezo' (stumbling), hin 'ठोकर-का' (stumbling), arb 'عَثرَةٍ' (stumbling-block), kor '부딪침의' (collision), swa 'kujikwaa' (stumbling). Found in Isa 8:14.
